title: kithctl contacts list
description:
Implement kithctl contacts list: open SQLite database read-only, list contacts table in tabular format.

WHAT: Print all contacts (login, display name, mailbox host, blocked status, last seen) so operators can verify who has been auto-added.

ALGORITHM:
1. Build Config from env + CLI overrides; derive db_path = config.db_path()
2. Verify db_path exists: if not, eprintln!("error: database not found at {path}: run kithd first") and exit(1)
3. Open: Store::open(&db_path) — on Err: eprintln! and exit(1)
4. Call store.contacts().list()? → Vec<Contact>
5. If empty: println!("No contacts.") and return Ok(())
6. Print table header: "LOGIN                          DISPLAY NAME              MAILBOX HOST                             BLOCKED  LAST SEEN"
7. Print separator line of dashes matching header width
8. For each contact: println!("{:<30} {:<25} {:<40} {:<8} {}",
     contact.login_or_fallback(), display_or_dash, contact.mailbox_host, blocked_str, contact.last_seen_at)
   where login_or_fallback = contact.login if non-empty else contact.tailscale_user_id
   where display_or_dash = contact.display_name.as_deref().unwrap_or("-")
   where blocked_str = if contact.blocked { "BLOCKED" } else { "ok" }
9. println!("") then println!("{} contact(s)", contacts.len())

DEFENSIVE RULES:
- Display name may be None — use "-" not panic
- login may be empty (Headscale without OIDC) — fall back to tailscale_user_id
- Do not print internal IDs (contact.id field) — they are opaque store keys
- last_seen_at is a pre-formatted RFC 3339 string from kith-store; just print it
- Store::open opens read-write even for reads; this is safe (WAL mode, no writes done)

TESTS:
- Integration test: create temp SQLite file using Store::open_in_memory() or a temp file, insert 2 contacts via ContactStore::upsert(), run contacts list logic, assert output contains both login names. Oracle: manually constructed expected output strings.
- Test with empty DB: assert output is exactly "No contacts."
